evidence.observation: Automatic retention is the only server-side edge into 'archived'. The per-project loop (lines 162-196) derives terminalStatus from status==='success'||'failed'||'fail' and gates archival on terminalExpired (now-terminalAt >= FINAL_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS), restoredExpired (status==='archived' && restoredAt>0 && now-restoredAt >= RESTORED_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS) or archivedNeedsUnload (status==='archived' && restoredAt===0 && hasLoadedAgent). Anything else is pushed to `skipped`/`kept` (line 178). So allowed automation edges are terminal->archived and archived(re-restored/cold-with-loaded-agents)->archived; every non-terminal or fresh-terminal status is a forbidden edge into archived.

Implements the explicit allowed edge archived->restored. It re-creates only missing members via wattclaw.team.project.member.update (lines 225-237), throws if any project agent is still missing (lines 247-249), and returns `restored: projectStatus(currentProject) === 'archived'` (line 254). It is never invoked automatically by the retention pass, which confirms restore is a user-triggered transition rather than part of pruning.

Retention windows that parameterise the allowed/forbidden edges: FINAL_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS = 3 days for terminal success/failed projects, RESTORED_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS = 24h before a restored archive may be archived again, and SHANGHAI_UTC_OFFSET_MS used by nextWattClawRetentionRunAt to schedule the daily 18:00 Asia/Shanghai retention run that evaluates those edges.

Normalises project.status (trim + lowercase) into the canonical state token used by every transition predicate, so the state machine is case/whitespace insensitive; the same statuses observed here (success, failed/fail, archived, in_progress, pending) map onto the WattClawProjectStatus union in src/api/types/wattclaw-team.ts.

Forbidden-edge enforcement on the client. On a wattclaw.team.project.updated event the guard `if (archivedProjectIds.has(targetProjectId) && nextStatus !== 'archived') return` (line 334) makes archived a sink: a Gateway update can never move an archived project to any non-archived status. Line 335 latches the archived set, and the same id is re-added whenever listWattClawProjects reports status 'archived' (loadSavedProjectsMeta, line 903).

Confirms archived is not auto-restored: when the loaded project status is 'archived' (line 699) the store binds the manager session read-only and returns without calling activateWattClawProject, so archived->restored (or archived->in_progress) is forbidden automatically and requires the explicit restoreProject action.

The explicit allowed edge archived->restored: it calls RPC activateWattClawProject, replaces the project status with 'restored' when the previous status was archived (line 749), clears the archived latch, sets runtimeReady=true and persists the metadata. prepareOutgoingMessage (line ~515) separately throws for archived projects, blocking an archived->in_progress interaction edge.

Manual archive/restore edge set. ARCHIVABLE_STATUSES = {success, fail, failed, paused, restored} plus canArchive means only finished projects may transition to archived by hand (in_progress/pending/creating/planning/waiting cannot). canRestore is true only when status==='archived' && !runtimeReady, restricting the restore edge to an explicit, runtime-down archived project.

claims.claim: Allowed edge success/failed/fail -> archived: terminal projects are archived by the automatic retention pass only after FINAL_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS (3 days) since updatedAt/createdAt; fresh terminal projects are kept.

Allowed edge archived -> restored: activateWattClawProjectRuntime restores missing project members and returns restored:true when the project status is 'archived'; the client performs this only on explicit user action via restoreProject, not during initialize or realtime updates.

Forbidden edge archived -> any non-archived status: handleRealtimeEvent rejects Gateway updates that would move a latched archived project away from 'archived', initialize skips runtime activation for archived projects, and prepareOutgoingMessage throws, so the only legal exit from archived is an explicit restore.

Forbidden edge in_progress/pending/planning/creating/waiting/paused -> archived via automation: these are non-terminal, so the retention loop never calls wattclaw.team.project.archive on them and pushes them to kept/skipped.

Allowed manual-archive edge {success, fail, failed, paused, restored} -> archived, and manual restore edge archived -> restored, are exposed and constrained by ARCHIVABLE_STATUSES and canRestore in the project panel; paused is archivable only manually because retention treats it as non-terminal.

Allowed self-edge archived -> archived (re-archive/unload): retention re-archives an archived project when it was restored more than 24h ago (restoredExpired) or when it still has loaded agents after a cold archive (archivedNeedsUnload); an archived project whose agents are already unloaded and never restored is forbidden from re-archiving and is kept.

conclusion.state_machine: Project lifecycle states observed: creating, waiting, pending, planning, in_progress (a.k.a. running), paused, success, failed/fail (terminal), archived, restored. Status is normalised with trim().toLowerCase() (projectStatus) and typed by WattClawProjectStatus in src/api/types/wattclaw-team.ts.
allowed_edges: creating -> waiting | pending | planning (draft/creation flow; 'pending' gates the start-confirmation UI)
pending | planning | waiting | creating -> in_progress (project start)
{success, failed} -> archived (automatic retention after 3 days: FINAL_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS)
{success, fail, failed, paused, restored} -> archived (explicit manual archive, ARCHIVABLE_STATUSES)
archived -> restored (explicit user action, only when runtime is not ready; activateWattClawProjectRuntime returns restored:true)
archived -> archived (retention re-archive: restored >24h ago, or still has loaded agents -> forced unload)
forbidden_edges: archived -> {creating, waiting, pending, planning, in_progress, paused, success, failed}: blocked by the realtime archived latch, by initialize (no auto-activation), and by prepareOutgoingMessage
{success, failed} -> in_progress/pending (no resurrection of terminal projects)
fresh terminal {success, failed} -> archived (younger than 3 days: kept)
{in_progress, pending, planning, creating, waiting, paused} -> archived by retention (non-terminal: kept/skipped; paused is manual-only)
archived (restoredAt within 24h) -> archived (restoredExpired not reached, kept)
conclusion.summary: The lifecycle is a forward pipeline that ends in the archived sink. Terminal outcomes (success/failed/fail) may flow to archived automatically after a 3-day retention window or manually at any time; paused and restored are only archivable manually; a restored archive may be re-archived after 24h, and a cold archive whose agents are still loaded is force-unloaded. The single legal exit from archived is the explicit archived->restored user action; no realtime event, initial page load, or retention pass may take an archived project out of that state, and no non-terminal project may be archived by automation.
